note: After-release measurement for #353 (holding back session start and read delivery to agent-started runs, and the search line only at subagent starts), shipped in 0.6.61 on 2026-10-18. The plan fixed the window as 7 days from the day after publication (UTC). Counted 2026-10-27 from the owner's database (read only) and Claude Code and Codex transcripts. counts.after_release is server/evals/delivery/after-release.ts for 2026-10-09..16 and this window; counts.per_session takes as denominator the sessions with an owner message in the window, delivered or not. Labels by Claude and Codex independently; a disagreement is unknown. Claude labelled from a shortened view of the sheet (record, request, last 2 lines before, first 10 and last 3 lines after, long lines cut); Codex read the full sheet. No bar was fixed: the plan asks for counts by recipient.

sampling.method: pinned pairs ordered by delivery time, delivery id, unit id, shuffled with mulberry32, first 80 (server/evals/delivery/sample.ts --sample)

labels.useful: the record's content bears on what the agent was doing at that moment: it stops a change that goes against it, tells a condition the work must keep, or helps avoid a known failure
labels.irrelevant: it has nothing to do with the work at that moment
labels.unknown: undecided, no transcript, or the two labellers disagree

after_release.note: Counts per window of what the #353 change did: held starts by recipient, Codex exec or log-less runs that still got their start or a read other than a dead-end stop (not_held), subagent and child-thread starts that still carried records, and pairs per interactive session. Recipients come from the delivery row and the Codex session log, as in agent-runs.ts: no log tells a claude -p run from a person's Claude Code session, so one that was not held counts as interactive, and a window before the release counts what the change would have held as not_held.
